# Overview

```{r model_family_header, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
acousticTS:::.model_family_header(
  family = "hpa",
  pages = c(
    Overview = "index.html",
    Implementation = "hpa-implementation.html",
    Theory = "hpa-theory.html"
  )
)
```

```{r hpa_overview, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
acousticTS:::.model_family_overview(
  family = "hpa",
  summary = paste(
    "The high-pass approximation (`HPA`) provides fast broadband estimates",
    "for simple fluid-like canonical bodies by joining low-frequency and",
    "reflection-controlled high-frequency behaviour."
  ),
  core_idea = paste(
    "Use a rational form that recovers the Rayleigh-scale response at small",
    "acoustic size while limiting its high-frequency growth. The Johnson method",
    "is sphere-specific, while the Stanton method also covers prolate spheroids",
    "and cylinders [@Johnson_1977; @Stanton_1989_1]."
  ),
  best_for = c(
    "Rapid broadband trend calculations for spheres, prolate spheroids, and cylinders",
    "Screening shape, size, orientation, or material-contrast effects",
    "Comparison with a geometry-matched modal solution when fine resonances are not required"
  ),
  supports = c(
    "The Johnson sphere and Stanton sphere, prolate-spheroid, and cylinder formulations",
    "Fluid-like density and sound-speed contrasts relative to the exterior medium",
    "Optional null-position and deviation controls"
  ),
  assumptions = c(
    "An interpolation formula rather than an exact boundary-value solution",
    "A supported canonical shape and the source formulation's geometric prefactors",
    "No complete modal resonance structure",
    "Results are interpreted over the approximation's acoustic-size regime"
  ),
  reading = c(
    "[Implementation](hpa-implementation.html): method selection, supported shapes, output, and comparisons",
    "[Theory](hpa-theory.html): low-frequency term, reflection limit, and shape-specific forms"
  )
)
```
